findings.text: FINDING imas_ambix/agent/provider_prices.py:370 follow-on: _rates duplicates the capability imas_ambix/agent/watch.py:278 already owns -- the same returned keys (prompt, cache_read, completion) and the same cache-read-falls-back-to-the-prompt-rate rule -- and does not extend that owner; watch already reaches provider_prices through a lazy import, so the normaliser could have lived here and been imported by watch rather than copied, and the copy now has to be kept in step by hand.

FINDING imas_ambix/agent/provider_prices.py:121 follow-on: the recovered 2026-10-02 row's citation states '22.0 G input and 166 M output tokens' where the plan source it cites (docs/plans/serving-record-warehouse.html:778) states 22.8 B input and 0.166 B output; the output figure is equivalent but the input figure differs (22.0 against 22.8), so the provenance a reader is told to check does not reconcile with the source, and the rate it justifies (1.37e-08, correctly one millionth of the plan's per-million figure) rests on a citation that has been silently altered.

FINDING imas_ambix/agent/provider_prices.py:559 follow-on: the endpoints change test compares the whole json.dumps of the listing, so a listing whose endpoints are merely reordered -- or whose provider metadata changes while every price is unchanged -- appends a history row even though nothing repriced; the plan frames the file as growing with price changes rather than fetches, so the row is not the change it claims to record. The median reader is order-independent, so the extra row is benign to consumers but it inflates the history the change exists to keep minimal.
